'''Léon-François-Antoine Aurifeuille''' (1822–1882) was a French [[mathematician]] after whom [[Aurifeuillean factorization]]s are named.<ref>{{citation|first=David|last=Wells|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1MTcYrbTdsUC&pg=PA15|title=Prime Numbers: The Most Mysterious Figures in Math|page=15|year=2005|isbn=0-471-46234-9|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.|location=Hoboken, NJ}}.</ref>

He was the author of three books: ''Cours de géométrie élémentaire'' (with C. Richaud, Paris: Bachelier, 1847),
''Traité de géométrie élémentaire'' (with C. Dumont, 2nd ed., Toulouse: Bonnal & Gibrac, 1860), and ''Traité d'arithmétique'' (with C. Dumont, 2nd ed., Toulouse: Bonnal & Gibrac, 1859).<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=zhQ2AQAAMAAJ&pg=RA1-PA590&lpg=RA1-PA590 Catalogue général des livres imprimés de la Bibliothèque nationale], Vol. 5, pp. 590–591, 1900.</ref>

Under the [[pseudonym]] '''Alfred de Caston''',<ref>[http://data.bnf.fr/16256309/alfred_de_caston/ Alfred de Caston], French National Library, retrieved 2015-03-05.</ref> he also wrote several other books, including ''Les Tricheurs, scènes de jeu'' (Paris: E. Dentu, 1863) and ''Les marchands de miracles; histoire de la superstition humaine'' (Paris: E. Dentu, 1864).
